arxiv-2202-11172.title: The First Measurement of the Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment from the Fermilab Muon g − 2 g-2 Collaboration
arxiv-2202-11172.creator: A. Tewsley-Booth on behalf of the Muon g − 2 g-2 Collaboration
arxiv-2202-11172.description: Abstract This paper will cover the physics and methods behind Fermilab’s Muon g-2 Experiment, along with the long-awaited results from Run-1. The experiment was undertaken to resolve the tension between the Standard Model and the previous measurement taken at Brookhaven National Laboratory.

arxiv-2206-12120.title: Photoproduction of J / ψ J/\psi in d+Au ultraperipheral collisions at the BNL Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider
arxiv-2206-12120.creator: V. Guzey, E. Kryshen, M. Strikman, M. Zhalov
arxiv-2206-12120.description: Abstract We argue that the STAR data on J / ψ J/\psi photoproduction in d + A ​ u d+Au ultraperipheral collisions (UPCs) at the momentum transfer t ≠ 0 t\neq 0 primarily probes elastic and possibly nucleon-dissociative J / ψ J/\psi photoproduction on quasi-free nucleons, while being essentially insensitive to expectedly weak nuclear modifications of the gluon distribution in

arxiv-2207-03347.title: Thermodynamics of Hot Neutron Stars and Universal Relations
arxiv-2207-03347.creator: Pavlos Laskos-Patkos, Polychronis S. Koliogiannis, Alkiviadis Kanakis-Pegios, Charalampos C. Moustakidis
arxiv-2207-03347.description: Abstract Over the last few years, the detection of gravitational waves from binary neutron star systems has rekindled our hopes for a deeper understanding of the unknown nature of ultradense matter. In particular, gravitational wave constraints on the tidal deformability of a neutron star can be translated into constraints on several neutron star properties using a set of universal relations.

arxiv-2211-07306.creator: Razieh Emami, Richard Anantua, Angelo Ricarte, Sheperd S. Doeleman, Avery Broderick, George Wong, Lindy Blackburn, Maciek Wielgus, Ramesh Narayan, Grant Tremblay, Charles Alcock, Lars Hernquist, Randall Smith, Matthew Liska, Priyamvada Natarajan, Mark Vogelsberger, Brandon Curd, Joana A. Kramer
arxiv-2211-07306.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Razieh Emami, Richard Anantua, Angelo Ricarte, Sheperd S. Doeleman, Avery Broderick, George Wong, Lindy Blackburn, Maciek Wielgus, Ramesh Narayan, Grant Tremblay, Charles Alcock, Lars Hernquist, Randall Smith, Matthew Liska, Priyamvada Natarajan, Mark Vogelsberger, Brandon Curd, Joana A. Kramer. arxiv-2302-06252.title: Near-Optimal Dynamic Time Warping on Run-Length Encoded Strings
arxiv-2302-06252.creator: Itai Boneh, Shay Golan, Shay Mozes, Oren Weimann
arxiv-2302-06252.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Itai Boneh, Shay Golan, Shay Mozes, Oren Weimann. We give an O ~ ​ ( n 2 ) \tilde{O}(n^{2}) time algorithm for computing the exact Dynamic Time Warping distance between two strings whose run-length encoding is of size at most n n .

arxiv-2303-02200.title: No MSP Counterparts Detected in GBT Searches of Spider Candidates 4FGL J0935.3+0901, 4FGL J1627.7+3219, and 4FGL J2212.4+0708 Facilities: Robert C. Byrd Green Bank Telescope (GBT) PRESTO ( Ransom 2011 ) , psrfits_utils
arxiv-2303-02200.creator: Kyle A. Corcoran, Scott M. Ransom, Ryan S. Lynch
arxiv-2303-02200.description: Abstract We performed radio searches for the “spider” millisecond pulsar (MSP) candidates 4FGL J0935.3+0901, 4FGL J1627.7+3219, and 4FGL J2212.4+0708 using the Green Bank Telescope in an attempt to detect the proposed radio counterpart of the multi-wavelength variability seen in each system.

arxiv-2305-04257.title: Unrolled Architectures for High-Throughput Encoding of Multi-Kernel Polar Codes PubID: pubid: 0000–0000/00$00.00 © 2023 IEEE
arxiv-2305-04257.creator: Hossein Rezaei, Elham Abbasi, Nandana Rajatheva, Matti Latva-aho
arxiv-2305-04257.description: Abstract Over the past decade, polar codes have received significant traction and have been selected as the coding method for the control channel in fifth-generation (5G) wireless communication systems. However, conventional polar codes are reliant solely on binary ( 2 × 2 2\times 2 ) kernels, which restricts their block length to being only powers of 2 2 .

arxiv-2306-17694.title: Gap-Dependent Hydrodynamic Lubrication in Conformal Contacts
arxiv-2306-17694.creator: James A. Richards, Patrick B. Warren, Wilson C. K. Poon
arxiv-2306-17694.description: Abstract We show that the hydrodynamic lubrication of contacting conformal surfaces with a typical texture height gives rise to a universal behaviour in the Stribeck curve in which the friction coefficient shows an anomalous power-law dependence on the Sommerfeld number, μ ∼ S 2 / 3 \mu\sim S^{2/3} .

arxiv-2409-17669.title: Impact of opinion formation phenomena in epidemic dynamics: kinetic modeling on networks
arxiv-2409-17669.creator: G. Albi, E. Calzola, G. Dimarco, M. Zanella
arxiv-2409-17669.description: Abstract After the recent COVID-19 outbreaks, it became increasingly evident that individuals’ thoughts and beliefs can have a strong impact on disease transmission. It becomes therefore important to understand how information and opinions on protective measures evolve during epidemics. To this end, incorporating the impact of social media is essential to take into account the hierarchical structure of these platforms.

arxiv-2410-01941.title: Stochastic resetting prevails over sharp restart for broad target distributions
arxiv-2410-01941.creator: Martin R. Evans, Somrita Ray
arxiv-2410-01941.description: Abstract Resetting has been shown to reduce the completion time for a stochastic process, such as the first passage time for a diffusive searcher to find a target. The time between two consecutive resetting events is drawn from a waiting time distribution ψ ⁡ ( t ) \psi(t) , which defines the resetting protocol.

arxiv-2502-04506.title: When One LLM Drools, Multi-LLM Collaboration Rules
arxiv-2502-04506.creator: Shangbin Feng, Wenxuan Ding, Alisa Liu, Zifeng Wang, Weijia Shi, Yike Wang, Shannon Zejiang Shen, Xiaochuang Han, Hunter Lang, Chen-Yu Lee, Tomas Pfister, Yejin Choi, Yulia Tsvetkov
arxiv-2502-04506.description: Abstract This position paper argues that in many realistic (i.e., complex, contextualized, subjective) scenarios, one LLM is not enough to produce a reliable output. We challenge the status quo of relying solely on a single general-purpose LLM and argue for multi-LLM collaboration to better represent the extensive diversity of data, skills, and people.

arxiv-2506-10961.title: Discovery and Localization of the Swift-Observed FRB 20241228A in a Star-forming Host Galaxy Facilities: CHIME, KKO, GBO, Gemini (GMOS) Fitburst , PATH , ffff-pz , Marz , CIGALE

Cook, Fengqiu Adam Dong, Yuxin Dong, Tarraneh Eftekhari, Wen-fai Fong, Emmanuel Fonseca, Jason W. T. Hessels, Ronniy C. Joseph, Victoria Kaspi, Calvin Leung, Robert Main, Kiyoshi W. Masui, Ryan Mckinven, Da
arxiv-2506-10961.description: Abstract On 2024 December 28, CHIME/FRB detected the thus-far non-repeating FRB 20241228A with a real-time signal-to-noise ratio of > 50 >50 . Approximately 112 s later, the X-ray Telescope onboard the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory was on source, the fastest follow-up to-date of a non-repeating FRB (Tohuvavohu et al. in prep. ).

arxiv-2506-12839.title: Fair Bayesian Model-Based Clustering
arxiv-2506-12839.creator: Jihu Lee, Kunwoong Kim, Yongdai Kim
arxiv-2506-12839.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jihu Lee, Kunwoong Kim, Yongdai Kim. Fair clustering has become a socially significant task with the advancement of machine learning technologies and the growing demand for trustworthy AI. Group fairness ensures that the proportions of each sensitive group are similar in all clusters. Most existing group-fair clustering methods are based on the K K -means clustering and thus require the distance between instances and the number of clusters to be given in advance.

arxiv-2508-21004.title: Lethe: Purifying Backdoored Large Language Models with Knowledge Dilution
arxiv-2508-21004.creator: Chen Chen, Yuchen Sun, Jiaxin Gao, Xueluan Gong, Qian Wang, Ziyao Wang, Yongsen Zheng, Kwok-Yan Lam
arxiv-2508-21004.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have seen significant advancements, achieving superior performance in various Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks. However, they remain vulnerable to backdoor attacks, where models behave normally for standard queries but generate harmful responses or unintended output when specific triggers are activated.

arxiv-2511-00656.title: Diode effect in a skyrmion-coupled high-temperature Josephson junction
arxiv-2511-00656.creator: Digvijay Singh, Pankaj Sharma, Narayan Mohanta
arxiv-2511-00656.description: Abstract We show that a planar Josephson junction having d d -wave superconducting regions, with a skyrmion crystal placed underneath, produces a robust gate-tunable superconducting diode effect. The spatially-varying exchange field of the skyrmion crystal breaks both inversion and time-reversal symmetries, leading to an asymmetric current-phase relation with an anomalous phase shift.

europmc-pmc7574920.title: A colorimetric RT-LAMP assay and LAMP-sequencing for detecting SARS-CoV-2 RNA in clinical samples.
europmc-pmc7574920.creator: Dao Thi VL, Herbst K, Boerner K, Meurer M, Kremer LP, Kirrmaier D, Freistaedter A, Papagiannidis D, Galmozzi C, Stanifer ML, Boulant S, Klein S, Chlanda P, Khalid D, Barreto Miranda I, Schnitzler P, Kräusslich HG, Knop M, Anders S.
europmc-pmc7574920.description: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic caused by the SARS-CoV-2 (severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2) coronavirus is a major public health challenge. Rapid tests for detecting existing SARS-CoV-2 infections and assessing virus spread are critical....

pmc-10737212.title: PHARMACOLOGIC AMPK ACTIVATION IMPROVES HEALTHSPAN AND LIFESPAN IN NORMAL AND PREMATURE AGING MODELS
pmc-10737212.creator: Ozlem Altintas Akin, Sarah Mitchell, Shana Sturla, Michael MacArthur
pmc-10737212.description: Cockayne Syndrome (CS) is a rare autosomal recessive childhood disease, caused by mutations in CSA (ERCC8) or CSB (ERCC6) genes leading to defective DNA damage repair. CS characteristics include UV sensitivity and premature aging. Deficiencies in CSA or CSB may lead to impaired AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) activation. Notably, AMPK-activating interventions have shown promise in preclinical CS mouse models.

pmc-13002391.title: Application of convolutional neural networks for automated segmentation and classification in esophageal diseases
pmc-13002391.creator: Liangpeng Pu, Xiao Wang, Shanshan Yan, Shuaishuai Zhuang, Xiaopu He
pmc-13002391.description: ObjectiveTo develop a convolutional neural network (CNN) framework for the automated segmentation and classification of esophageal lesions in endoscopic images.Methods(1) Lesion localization was performed using a Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (R-CNN). (2) A dual-stream Esophageal Lesion Network (ELNet) was developed to classify images into four diagnostic categories. (3) Lesion segmentation was carried out using an ensemble of three U-Net architectures.

pmc-13017753.title: Inferring genotype–phenotype maps using attention models
pmc-13017753.creator: Krishna Rijal, Caroline M Holmes, Samantha Petti, Gautam Reddy, Michael M Desai, Pankaj Mehta, Panayiotis Benos
pmc-13017753.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Predicting phenotype from genotype is a central challenge in genetics. Traditional approaches in quantitative genetics typically analyze this problem using methods based on linear regression. These methods generally assume that the genetic architecture of complex traits can be parameterized in terms of an additive model, where the effects of loci are independent, plus (in some cases) pairwise epistatic interactions between loci. However, these models struggle to analyze more complex patterns of epistasis or subtle gene–environment interactions.

pmc-13185784.title: Current and emerging antibacterial strategies for periprosthetic joint infection: An overview
pmc-13185784.creator: Marco Fosca, Veronica Manescu, Iulian Antoniac, Julietta V. Rau
pmc-13185784.description: Periprosthetic Joint Infection (PJI) represents one of the most serious complications following joint arthroplasty, with impactful consequences in the clinic and economy. Characterized by biofilm formation on implant surfaces, PJI poses significant therapeutic challenges due to the limited efficacy of systemic antibiotics and the increasing prevalence of multidrug-resistant bacteria.

pmc-13264061.title: Process Improvement Before Artificial Intelligence and Automation: Building Trust With the Understand-Transform-Sustain Framework
pmc-13264061.creator: Alejandro Fabrega Gerbaud, Marta Berguido de la Guardia, Sandra C. Booth, LaRissa Adams, Matthew D. Cox, Kimberly Hunsinger, Nelly Tan, Melissa Gulden, Terri Menser, Ross Reichard, Sean C. Dowdy, Pablo Moreno Franco
pmc-13264061.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) and automation are rapidly transforming health care, yet their integration into clinical workflows often falls short owing to technical, ethical, and organizational challenges. Lack of trust emerges as the central hurdle, encompassing both patient and provider confidence in AI systems.

pmc-13369937.title: Verifier-initiated quantum message-authentication via quantum zero-knowledge proofs
pmc-13369937.creator: Wusheng Wang, Masahito Hayashi
pmc-13369937.description: On-demand authentication is critical for scalable quantum systems, yet many existing quantum signature and message-authentication schemes are signer-initiated, requiring advance distribution of authentication material even when no verification occurs. We introduce verifier-initiated quantum digital signatures (VIQDS), in which the verifier requests authentication only when needed and the signer responds once; after issuance, verification proceeds without further interaction.

pmc-13461561.title: Prepared or at-risk? Evaluating live viral vaccine coverage and vaccine immunogenicity before pediatric solid organ transplantation
pmc-13461561.creator: Benhur Sirvan Cetin, Caitlin Brammer, William Otto, Kerrigan Perkins, Teresa Ambrosino, Hilary Miller-Handley, Mark Murphy, Grant Paulsen, Emily Cain, Kathleen Campbell, Lara Danziger-Isakov

pmc-13564118.title: From cyberbullying to criminal liability: Digital forensic markers in cases of suspected abetment to suicide
pmc-13564118.creator: Nurzhan Saulen, Almas Kanatovich Kanatov, Zhauhar Kenesbaevna Kozhantayeva, Orynbassar Tlepbergenov, Dinara Osmanova
pmc-13564118.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cyberbullying that escalates into a victim's suicide poses significant challenges at the intersection of criminal law, causation analysis, and digital forensics. This article aims to examine how four jurisdictions - Kazakhstan, the United States, Germany, and India - conceptualise and assign criminal liability for suspected abetment to suicide conducted through online harassment, and to identify the evidentiary thresholds that shape prosecutorial decision-making.Methodscomprise comparative doctrinal analysis of legislation and published judgments, supplemented by structured document analysis of official materials and digital-evidence standards.

pmc-13605055.title: Molecular Pathogenesis, Tumor Microenvironment and Health Disparities in Select Pediatric Solid Tumors: An Integrative Narrative Review
pmc-13605055.creator: MiaSara Pérez-Salvá, Carolyn M. Ruiz-Pérez, Alondra Veloz-Bonilla, Rocío K. Rivera-Valentín
pmc-13605055.description: Background/Objectives: Pediatric solid tumors (PST) are a biologically distinct group of malignancies whose developmental origins and molecular drivers differ substantially from those of adult cancers, with direct implications for therapeutic strategy and clinical outcome. This review synthesizes current evidence on molecular pathogenesis, tumor microenvironment biology, and the structural conditions that shape access to care across select PST.
